30.2.s: tāny acyutāni syur iti ha eka āhuḥ savana dharaṇāni iti vadantaḥ |
30.2.d: तान्य् अच्युतानि स्युर् इति ह एक आहुः सवन धरणानि इति वदन्तः |

30.2.s: anyāny anyāni iti tv eva sthitam |
30.2.d: अन्यान्य् अन्यानि इति त्व् एव स्थितम् |

30.2.s: anyad anyadd hy ahar upayanti |
30.2.d: अन्यद् अन्यद्द् ह्य् अहर् उपयन्ति |

30.2.s: atha vāruṇam bārhaspatyam vaiṣṇavam iti śaṃsanti |
30.2.d: अथ वारुणम् बार्हस्पत्यम् वैष्णवम् इति शंसन्ति |

30.2.s: jagatī vā eteṣām chandas triṣṭub indrasya |
30.2.d: जगती वा एतेषाम् छन्दस् त्रिष्टुब् इन्द्रस्य |

30.2.s: tad yat chandasī viparīte dvidevatyāyai |
30.2.d: तद् यत् छन्दसी विपरीते द्विदेवत्यायै |

30.2.s: aindrāvaruṇam aindrā bārhaspatyam aindrāvaiṣṇavam iti śaṃsanti |
30.2.d: ऐन्द्रावरुणम् ऐन्द्रा बार्हस्पत्यम् ऐन्द्रावैष्णवम् इति शंसन्ति |

30.2.s: grahān eva etair anuśaṃsanti |
30.2.d: ग्रहान् एव एतैर् अनुशंसन्ति |

30.2.s: evam hi grahā gṛhītā bhavanti |
30.2.d: एवम् हि ग्रहा गृहीता भवन्ति |

30.2.s: carṣaṇī dhṛtam maghavānam ukthyam iti maitrāvaruṇas tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
30.2.d: चर्षणी धृतम् मघवानम् उक्थ्यम् इति मैत्रावरुणस् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |
30.2.e: 'Holder of the people, the generous, worthy of praise' the Maitrāvaruṇa (says); the explanation of this has been given. The conclusion is by Vasiṣṭha day by day; Vasiṣṭha saw the third pressing for the Maitrāvaruṇa's function; therefore day by day the conclusion is by Vasiṣṭha. In Kakubh verses they give the lead to the Maitrāvaruṇa on the third day; thereby he falls into the power of the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin. On the fourth day they give the lead to each in his own metre; verily thus each in his own metre they continue finding support. In Gāyatrī verses they give the lead to the Maitrāvaruṇa, in Uṣṇih verses to the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin, in Anuṣṭubh verses to the Achāvāka, to secure a progressive increase. So their metres increase with four syllables each. In Paṅkti verses they give the lead to the Maitrāvaruṇa on the fifth day, for the fifth day is connected with the Paṅkti; in (verses) of two Padas they give the lead on the sixth day, for the sixth day is connected with (verses) of two Padas. Moreover they perform the Sāmans, Gūrda, Bhadra, Udvaṅcaputra; moreover the Śilpas are accompanied by (verses) of two feet; therefore here the Śilpas are recited, (thinking) 'Let us not depart from the Śilpas.'

30.2.s: vāsiṣṭho ahar ahaḥ paryāso bhavati |
30.2.d: वासिष्ठो अहर् अहः पर्यासो भवति |

30.2.s: vasiṣṭho ha etan maitrāvaruṇīyāyai tṛtīya savanam dadarśa |
30.2.d: वसिष्ठो ह एतन् मैत्रावरुणीयायै तृतीय सवनम् ददर्श |

30.2.s: tasmād vāsiṣṭho ahar ahaḥ paryāso bhavati |
30.2.d: तस्माद् वासिष्ठो अहर् अहः पर्यासो भवति |

30.2.s: kakupsu maitrāvaruṇāya praṇayanti tṛtīye ahan |
30.2.d: ककुप्सु मैत्रावरुणाय प्रणयन्ति तृतीये अहन् |

30.2.s: teno sa brāhmaṇācchaṃsino vaśam eti |
30.2.d: तेनो स ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनो वशम् एति |

30.2.s: atha caturthe ahant sve sve chandasi praṇayanti |
30.2.d: अथ चतुर्थे अहन्त् स्वे स्वे छन्दसि प्रणयन्ति |

30.2.s: sve sva eva tac chandasi pratitiṣṭhanto yanti |
30.2.d: स्वे स्व एव तच् छन्दसि प्रतितिष्ठन्तो यन्ति |

30.2.s: gāyatrīṣu maitrāvaruṇāya praṇayanty uṣṇikṣu brāhmaṇācchaṃsine anuṣṭupsv acchāvākāya uttara uttaritāyai |
30.2.d: गायत्रीषु मैत्रावरुणाय प्रणयन्त्य् उष्णिक्षु ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिने अनुष्टुप्स्व् अच्छावाकाय उत्तर उत्तरितायै |

30.2.s: tathā eṣām caturbhiś caturbhir akṣaraiś chandāṃsy abhyudyanti |
30.2.d: तथा एषाम् चतुर्भिश् चतुर्भिर् अक्षरैश् छन्दांस्य् अभ्युद्यन्ति |

30.2.s: paṅktiṣu maitrāvaruṇāya praṇayanti pañcame ahan |
30.2.d: पङ्क्तिषु मैत्रावरुणाय प्रणयन्ति पञ्चमे अहन् |

30.2.s: pāṅktam hi pañcamam ahaḥ |
30.2.d: पाङ्क्तम् हि पञ्चमम् अहः |

30.3.s: atho gūrdam bhadram udvaṃśa putram iti sāmāni kurvanti |
30.3.d: अथो गूर्दम् भद्रम् उद्वंश पुत्रम् इति सामानि कुर्वन्ति |

30.3.s: atho dvipadā sahacarāṇi vai śilpāni bhavanti |
30.3.d: अथो द्विपदा सहचराणि वै शिल्पानि भवन्ति |

30.3.e:
With the Nābhānediṣṭha the Hotṛ sprinkles seed; it he hands to the Maitrāvaruṇa; it he develops with the Vālakhilyās; these Vālakhilyās he recites as divided; by Padas the first two hymns he divides; verily thus
by joints he gathers him together; by half verses the second two; man consists of two portions; verily thus he unites them; verse by verse the third two hymns; verily thus he gathers him whole; he should invert in the Nārāśaṁsa; therefore foetuses are born inverted.

In the Tārkṣya he mounts the difficult mounting; Tārkṣya is Vāyu; Vāyu is breath verily thus he places breath in him; him he hands over to the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin. Him he receives in the womb of the Sukīrti (hymn ); for him born he recites in Paṅkti form with repetition of o the Vṛṣākapi (hymn); the repetition of o is food; verily thus born he finds support in proper food. Then he recites the Kuntāpa according to the metres, for the obtaining of all desires; viz. the Nārāśaṅsīs, the Raibhīs, the Kāravyās, the Indragāthās, the Bhūtechads, the Parikṣit verses, and the prattle of Etaśa. Etaśa, the sage, saw the life of the sacrifice. He said to his sons 'My boys, I have seen the life of the sacrifice; that I shall prattle forth; think me not mad.' They said 'Be it so.' Then he prattled it forth; his eldest son, creeping up, stopped his mouth, (saying) 'Our father has become mad.' To him he said 'Be gone; fie on thee, O fool; I make thine offspring the worst; hadst thou not, O fool, stopped my mouth, I had made the cow of a hundred (years of) life, and man of a thousand.' Therefore the descendants of Etaśa being the Ājāneyas are the worst of the Bhṛgus, for they are under curse by a father, their own deity, their own Prajāpati.

30.4.s: tam sa sukīrtinā yoninā pragigṛhṇāti jātam |
30.4.d: तम् स सुकीर्तिना योनिना प्रगिगृह्णाति जातम् |

30.4.s: atha etam vṛṣākapim paṅkti śaṃsam śaṃsati |
30.4.d: अथ एतम् वृषाकपिम् पङ्क्ति शंसम् शंसति |

30.4.s: jāta eva asmiṃs tad anna adyam pratidadhāti |
30.4.d: जात एव अस्मिंस् तद् अन्न अद्यम् प्रतिदधाति |

30.4.s: atha etat kuntāpam yathā chandasam śaṃsati |
30.4.d: अथ एतत् कुन्तापम् यथा छन्दसम् शंसति |

30.4.s: nārāśaṃsī raibhīḥ kāravyā indra gāthā bhūtecchadaḥ pārikṣitīr etaśa pralāpam iti |
30.4.d: नाराशंसी रैभीः कारव्या इन्द्र गाथा भूतेच्छदः पारिक्षितीर् एतश प्रलापम् इति |

30.4.s: etaśo ha vai munir yajñasya āyur dadarśa |
30.4.d: एतशो ह वै मुनिर् यज्ञस्य आयुर् ददर्श |

30.4.s: putrakā yajñasya āyur adarśam tad abhilapṣyāmi |
30.4.d: पुत्रका यज्ञस्य आयुर् अदर्शम् तद् अभिलप्ष्यामि |

30.4.s: tasya ha jyeṣṭhaḥ putro abhisṛpya mukham apijagrāha |
30.4.d: तस्य ह ज्येष्ठः पुत्रो अभिसृप्य मुखम् अपिजग्राह |

30.4.s: yad vai me jālma mukham na apy agrahīṣyaḥ |
30.4.d: यद् वै मे जाल्म मुखम् न अप्य् अग्रहीष्यः |

30.4.s: śata āyuṣam gām akariṣyam sahasra āyuṣam puruṣam iti |
30.4.d: शत आयुषम् गाम् अकरिष्यम् सहस्र आयुषम् पुरुषम् इति |

30.4.s: tasmād aitaśāyanā ājāneyāḥ santo bhṛgūṇām pāpiṣṭhāḥ pitrā abhiśaptāḥ svayā devatayā svena prajāpatinā |
30.4.d: तस्माद् ऐतशायना आजानेयाः सन्तो भृगूणाम् पापिष्ठाः पित्रा अभिशप्ताः स्वया देवतया स्वेन प्रजापतिना |

30.5.e:
(The verses) of the Ādityas and Aṅgirases he recites next. The Ādityas and the Aṅgirases were at variance, 'We shall go first to the world
of heaven' (said) the Āditya; 'we' the Aṅgirases. The Aṅgirases sent to the Ādityas (saying) 'Ours is the pressing day to-morrow; do ye cause us to sacrifice.' Agni was their envoy; the Ādityas said 'Ours is the pressing day to-day; and thou art the Hotṛ for us here, Bṛhaspati the Brahman, Ayāsya the Udgātṛ, Ghora Āṅgirasa the Ādhvaryu.' Them they rejected; him they desired to please with these (verses); thus they repeat these (verses). They brought a white horse as sacrificial fee, that one which here gives heat; therefore the Ādityas went to heaven; he goes to heaven who knows thus.

30.5.s: ādityāś ca ha vā aṅgirasaś ca aspardhanta |
30.5.d: आदित्याश् च ह वा अङ्गिरसश् च अस्पर्धन्त |

30.5.s: vayam pūrve svargam lokam eṣyāma ity ādityāḥ |
30.5.d: वयम् पूर्वे स्वर्गम् लोकम् एष्याम इत्य् आदित्याः |

30.5.s: śvaḥ sutyā no yājayata na iti |
30.5.d: श्वः सुत्या नो याजयत न इति |

30.5.s: teṣām nas tvam eva hotā asi |
30.5.d: तेषाम् नस् त्वम् एव होता असि |

30.5.s: bṛhaspatir brahmāya asya udgātā ghora āṅgiraso adhvaryur iti |
30.5.d: बृहस्पतिर् ब्रह्माय अस्य उद्गाता घोर आङ्गिरसो अध्वर्युर् इति |

30.5.s: te aśvam śvetam dakṣiṇām niṇyur etam eva ya eṣa tapati |
30.5.d: ते अश्वम् श्वेतम् दक्षिणाम् निण्युर् एतम् एव य एष तपति |

30.5.s: tata u ha ādityāḥ svar īyuḥ |
30.5.d: तत उ ह आदित्याः स्वर् ईयुः |

30.5.e: He recites the orderings of the quarters; the quarters are in order for him. He recites the man-ordering (verses); men are in order for him. He says the riddles, the Pratīrādhas, the Ativādā, the Āhanasyās, all forms of speech. Therefore a man speaks all forms of speech, but other animals one only. They are eight; by them the gods attained all attainments; so verily also the sacrificers by them attain all attainments. 'The Kapṛth, O men, the Kapṛth extend,' and 'What time forward ye came' are two (verses ); thus they become perfect. They make up ten; the Virāj consists of sets of ten; the Virāj is prosperity and proper food; verily (they serve) to obtain the Virāj as prosperity and proper food.

30.5.s: pravalhikāḥ pratīrādhān ativādām āhanasyāḥ sarvā vāco vadati |
30.5.d: प्रवल्हिकाः प्रतीराधान् अतिवादाम् आहनस्याः सर्वा वाचो वदति |

30.5.s: etābhir vai devāḥ sarvā aṣṭīr āśnuvata |
30.5.d: एताभिर् वै देवाः सर्वा अष्टीर् आश्नुवत |

30.5.s: tatho eva etad yajamānā etābhir eva sarvā aṣṭīr aśnuvate |
30.5.d: तथो एव एतद् यजमाना एताभिर् एव सर्वा अष्टीर् अश्नुवते |

30.5.s: kapṛnnaraḥ kapṛtham uddadhātana yadd ha prācīr ajagantā iti dve eka pātinyau |
30.5.d: कपृन्नरः कपृथम् उद्दधातन यद्द् ह प्राचीर् अजगन्ता इति द्वे एक पातिन्यौ |

30.5.e:
He recites the Dadhikrā (verse ); the Dadhikrā (verse) is speech; verily thus he places speech in him; he recites (the verses) to Soma the purifying; (the verses) to Soma the purifying are a filter; verily thus he purifies him. Him he hands over to the Achāvāka; him he with the
Evayāmarut (hymn ) makes to move when born; he repeats o; stumbling as it were one moves when first desirous to walk; verily thus from the immortal metre he propagates him for immortality; they obtain immortality who perform the sixth day (rite). Having recited the strophe and antistrophe, he recites the Vālakhilyās; the strophe and antistrophe are the body, the Vālakhilyās the breaths; these breaths are not separated (from the body). They say ‘Why are they (called) Vālakhilyās?’ That which is not in contact in two fields, they call Khila; these breaths are a hair (vāla) in breadth and are not separated; therefore are they Vālakhilyās.

30.6.s: nyūṅkha mānaka iva vai prathamam cicarṣaṃś carati |
30.6.d: न्यूङ्ख मानक इव वै प्रथमम् चिचर्षंश् चरति |

30.6.s: tad enam amṛtāc chandaso amṛtatvāya prajanayanti |
30.6.d: तद् एनम् अमृताच् छन्दसो अमृतत्वाय प्रजनयन्ति |

30.6.s: te amṛtatvam āpnuvanti ya ṣaṣṭham ahar upayanti |
30.6.d: ते अमृतत्वम् आप्नुवन्ति य षष्ठम् अहर् उपयन्ति |

30.6.s: anantarhitā u ha iem ātmanaḥ prāṇāḥ |
30.6.d: अनन्तर्हिता उ ह इएम् आत्मनः प्राणाः |

30.6.s: vāla mātrā u hi ime prāṇā asambhinnāḥ |
30.6.d: वाल मात्रा उ हि इमे प्राणा असम्भिन्नाः |

30.6.s: tārkṣye dūrohaṇam rohati iti tad uktam |
30.6.d: तार्क्ष्ये दूरोहणम् रोहति इति तद् उक्तम् |
30.6.e: ‘In the Tārkṣya he mounts the difficult mounting,’ it has been said. In Gāyatrī verses they give the lead for the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin on the second day, thereby he falls into the power of the Maitrāvaruṇa. ‘Forward to the most generous, the great, born of great wealth’ is a six verse (hymn ), twice as great as that of the Maitrāvaruṇa. The conclusion day by day is by Kṛṣṇa; Kṛṣṇa Āṅgirasa saw this third pressing for the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin’s office; therefore day by day the conclusion is by Kṛṣṇa. In Anuṣṭubhs they give the lead for the Achāvāka on the third day; thereby he falls into the power of the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin. The ‘season mother’ (hymn ) has thirteen verses; it is twice as great as that of the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin and there is one verse over. The conclusion day by day is by Bharadvāja; Bharadvāja saw this third pressing for the Achāvāka’s office; therefore day by day the conclusion is by Bharadvāja. The Achāvāka alternates the two Viṣṇu (hymns ), the conclusions the other two. The Maitrāvaruṇa and the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin have two conclusions; the Achāvāka has one conclusion. In that the Achāvāka has an unchanging conclusion, the Achāvāka is a support; verily (it serves) for support.

30.6.s: pra maṃhiṣṭhāya bṛhate bṛhad raya iti jāgatam ṣaḍṛcam tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
30.6.d: प्र मंहिष्ठाय बृहते बृहद् रय इति जागतम् षडृचम् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

30.6.s: kṛṣṇo ha etad āṅgiraso brāhmaṇācchaṃsīyāyai tṛtīya savanam dadarśa |
30.6.d: कृष्णो ह एतद् आङ्गिरसो ब्राह्मणाच्छंसीयायै तृतीय सवनम् ददर्श |

30.6.s: tasmād kārṣṇo ahar ahaḥ paryāso bhavati |
30.6.d: तस्माद् कार्ष्णो अहर् अहः पर्यासो भवति |

30.7.s: ṛtur janitrīyam trayodaśarcam tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
30.7.d: ऋतुर् जनित्रीयम् त्रयोदशर्चम् तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

30.7.s: dvis tāvad yāvad brāhmaṇācchaṃsina ekā ca upa |
30.7.d: द्विस् तावद् यावद् ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन एका च उप |

30.7.s: bharadvājo ha etad acchāvākīyāyai tṛtīya savanam dadarśa |
30.7.d: भरद्वाजो ह एतद् अच्छावाकीयायै तृतीय सवनम् ददर्श |

30.7.s: tasmād bhāradvājo ahar ahaḥ paryāso bhavati |
30.7.d: तस्माद् भारद्वाजो अहर् अहः पर्यासो भवति |

30.7.e:
Thirty-six (verses) the Maitrāvaruṇa recites at the Caturviṅśa, forty the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin, and forty-four the Achāvāka. These are a hundred and twenty. A hundred and twenty are the days of the season; thus he obtains the season, with the season the year and the desires that are in the year. Five hymns the Maitrāvaruṇa recites on all the Chandoma days; the Chandomas are cattle; cattle are fivefold; verily (they
serve) to obtain cattle. Four hymns the Brāhmaṇācchaṅsin recites in the first Chandoma; the Chandomas are cattle; cattle are fourfold, and also fourfooted; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. Five hymns the Achāvāka recites in the first Chandoma; the Chandomas are cattle; cattle are fivefold; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. Six (they recite) in the second and third; the year has six seasons; verily (they serve) to obtain the year. The Śastras have four calls; the litanies are cattle; cattle are fourfold, and also fourfooted; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. On the sixth day that of the Maitrāvaruṇa has five calls; the litanies are cattle; cattle are fivefold; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. The offering verses of the litanies are from the one day (rite); the one day (rite) is a support; verily (they serve) for support. They say the second vaṣaṭ, for the healing of the libations, for the support of the libations.

30.8.s: pañca pañca sūktāni tṛtīya savane maitrāvaruṇaḥ śaṃsati sarveṣu chandomeṣu |
30.8.d: पञ्च पञ्च सूक्तानि तृतीय सवने मैत्रावरुणः शंसति सर्वेषु छन्दोमेषु |

30.8.s: catvāri sūktāni brāhmaṇācchaṃsī śaṃsati prathame chandome |
30.8.d: चत्वारि सूक्तानि ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी शंसति प्रथमे छन्दोमे |

30.8.s: pañca sūktāny acchāvākaḥ śaṃsati prathame chandome |
30.8.d: पञ्च सूक्तान्य् अच्छावाकः शंसति प्रथमे छन्दोमे |

30.8.s: ṣaṣṭha eva ahan maitrāvaruṇasya pañca āhāvam bhavati |
30.8.d: षष्ठ एव अहन् मैत्रावरुणस्य पञ्च आहावम् भवति |

30.9.e:
Five metres they recite at night, Anuṣṭubh, Gāyatrī, Uṣṇih, Triṣṭubh and Jagatī; these are the metres of night. The night has five calls, and so the additional litany of the Vājapeya. ‘The night goes beyond the Uktha; verily thus from metre to metre they call’ Kauṣītaki used to say, to prevent sameness. In that he uses a Triṣṭubh containing the word ‘over the night’ as invitatory verse for the Aśvin litany cup, (it is because) the Praiṣa contains (the word) ‘over the night’, for the Somas are left over the night. Moreover, the Triṣṭubh is might and strength; verily thus might and strength he places in the sacrificer. The additional litanies of the Āptoryāma have four calls; the litanies are cattle; cattle are fourfold, and also fourfooted; verily (they serve) to obtain cattle. They use as concluding verses (verses) to the lord of the field, (thinking) ‘The field is this earth; in it undepressed shall we find support at the end’; verily thus in it undepressed do they find support at the end. In that the offering verses are Triṣṭubhs containing (the word) ‘over the night’, (it is) because the Somas are left over the night. Moreover, the Triṣṭubh is might and strength; verily thus might and strength he places in the sacrificer. They say the second vaṣaṭ, for the healing of the libations, for the support of the libations. They then proceed with (the cup) for the yoker of the bays; the
explanation of this has been given. He recites a Triṣṭubh as invitatory verse for (the cup) for the yoker of the bays; the explanation of this has been given. In that he recites an invitatory verse for the Atipraiṣa, (it is because) without strength is the Praiṣa which has no invitatory verse. Moreover there are invitatory verses in the case of (the cups) for two deities, and in the case of all the Prasthitas; therefore he recites an invitatory verse for it. ‘In that he recites an Atipraiṣa, verily thus he refers to the next day, verily thus they keep taking hold of the next day’ Kauṣītaki used to say.

30.9.s: anuṣṭubham gāyatrīm uṣṇiham triṣṭubham jagatīm iti |
30.9.d: अनुष्टुभम् गायत्रीम् उष्णिहम् त्रिष्टुभम् जगतीम् इति |

30.9.s: chandase chandasa eva tad āhvayanta iti ha sma āha kauṣītakir ajāmitāyai |
30.9.d: छन्दसे छन्दस एव तद् आह्वयन्त इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिर् अजामितायै |

30.9.s: atha yat tiro ahnyavatīm triṣṭubham āśvina iktha grahasya puronuvākyām anvāha |
30.9.d: अथ यत् तिरो अह्न्यवतीम् त्रिष्टुभम् आश्विन इक्थ ग्रहस्य पुरोनुवाक्याम् अन्वाह |

30.9.s: balam eva tad vīryam yajamāne dadhāti |
30.9.d: बलम् एव तद् वीर्यम् यजमाने दधाति |

30.9.s: asyām eva tad adīnāyām antataḥ pratitiṣṭhanti |
30.9.d: अस्याम् एव तद् अदीनायाम् अन्ततः प्रतितिष्ठन्ति |

30.9.s: atha yat tiro ahnyavatyas triṣṭubho yājyā bhavanti |
30.9.d: अथ यत् तिरो अह्न्यवत्यस् त्रिष्टुभो याज्या भवन्ति |

30.9.s: balam eva tad vīryam yajamāne dadhāti |
30.9.d: बलम् एव तद् वीर्यम् यजमाने दधाति |

30.9.s: atha hāriyojanena caranti tasya uktam brāhmaṇam |
30.9.d: अथ हारियोजनेन चरन्ति तस्य उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

30.9.s: triṣṭubham hāriyojanasya puronuvākyām anvāha tasyā uktam brāhmaṇam |
30.9.d: त्रिष्टुभम् हारियोजनस्य पुरोनुवाक्याम् अन्वाह तस्या उक्तम् ब्राह्मणम् |

30.9.s: avīryo ha vā u sa praiṣo yo apuronuvākhyaḥ |
30.9.d: अवीर्यो ह वा उ स प्रैषो यो अपुरोनुवाख्यः |

30.9.s: param eva etad ahar abhyārabhya vasanti iti ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ param eva etad ahar abhyārabhya vasanti iti ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ |
30.9.d: परम् एव एतद् अहर् अभ्यारभ्य वसन्ति इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः परम् एव एतद् अहर् अभ्यारभ्य वसन्ति इति ह स्म आह कौषीतकिः |
